items.title: 71231_Sam Wooding Oral History Interview
items.q: Tannhauser is a musical composition (opera by Wagner), not a person. The interviewee discusses performing arrangements of this work, indicating knowledge of the piece, not a personal relationship with an individual named Tannhauser.

ctx.x: Like, (sings Tannhauser). But at the same time, we would be using, (sings syncopated accompaniment). Things like that, with the saxophone. And it turned out well. Well, we had quite a number of them that we did. Some Rimsky-Korsakov, and one that we had was the "Overture of 1812". And we had it fixed so that you could actually hear the bells of Moscow and we had the drum beating so that now and then it was like the cannons, the Napoleonic cannons were shooting. And we did that up in a great way.
And as far as I know, nobody was doing that in this country.
